solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Long for British car that's small

indicators.note: 'X for Y' means one letter is put in place of another, here inside the car's name

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for long
B is the abbreviation for British, the letter to be replaced
the Volkswagen Beetle is a famous small car

explanation.surface: A motorist complains that a British car is long rather than compact.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the B of BEETLE for L to get LEETLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leetle is a jocular or dialect form of little, meaning tiny.

clue.text: Enter vehicle to get home, a rudimentary one

definitions.note: 'one' stands for the home just mentioned

parts.note: to log something is to enter it in a record
a cab is a taxi
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: Someone climbs into a taxi to get back to a very basic house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Home' does double duty: it supplies IN and is also what 'one' refers to in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A log cabin is a simple dwelling built from tree trunks, a basic kind of house.

clue.text: New ideas leader put out for forensic test

indicators.note: making something new reshapes it, so the remaining letters are rearranged
putting out the leader means the first letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A forensic scientist abandons the leading theory in favour of fresh ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the I from IDEAS and rearrange DEAS.
explanation.definitionFit: ESDA, electrostatic detection apparatus, is a laboratory method for revealing indented writing on documents.

clue.text: Romeo and a smitten former lover

indicators.note: smitten in its sense of struck hard suggests the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Romeo, besotted, is an ex-boyfriend from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smitten' reads as lovestruck, fitting Romeo, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamorado is an archaic word, from Spanish, for a sweetheart or admirer, so 'former' marks it as old usage.

clue.text: Nearly all having gone north lied about Murrayfield beating

indicators.note: in a down entry, going north means reading upwards, that is backwards
nearly means not quite whole, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about suggests letters turned around and moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rugby report: almost everyone heading north lied about a thrashing at Murrayfield.
explanation.walkthrough: Murrayfield is the Edinburgh rugby stadium, signalling a Scots word. Shorten ALL to AL, turn it upwards to LA, then add a rearranged LIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Laldie is Scots for a thrashing or punishment, so a beating in Scotland.

clue.text: Justification for absorbing mature port charges

indicators.note: absorbing means taking something in, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: grounds are reasons that justify an action
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a reason for a ship being charged extra for maturing port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the wine that matures, but it is the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundage is a fee paid by a ship for space while lying in harbour, hence plural port dues.

clue.text: Coarse snuff apparently in traditional Angus enclosure

indicators.note: in places one element inside the other, which surrounds it

parts.note: a ree is a Scots dialect word for a sheep pen; Angus is a Scottish county
APP is an abbreviation for apparently

explanation.surface: Tobacco snuff seems to be kept in an old Scottish farm enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: Angus is a Scottish county, so 'traditional Angus' flags an old Scots dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rappee is a strong, coarse kind of powdered tobacco taken by sniffing.

clue.text: Lacking respect, Independent MP sacked leaving obligations

indicators.note: being sacked means being thrown out, so those letters are removed

parts.note: impious means showing no reverence
I is the abbreviation for Independent
taken as written

explanation.surface: A disrespectful Independent member of parliament is fired and leaves behind debts.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I and MP from the start of IMPIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: IOUs are written acknowledgements of debt, so they are obligations to pay.

clue.text: Armed warriors clear, marches banned

indicators.note: marches are border areas, so banning them removes the outer letters

parts.note: limpid water is clear

explanation.surface: Armed fighters are cleared away as protest marches are prohibited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marches' looks like demonstrations; here it means borders, so LIMPID loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi is a body of Zulu warriors, an armed regiment.

clue.text: Upset one on bench

parts.note: 'un is a dialect form of one, as in 'a good 'un'
a settle is a long wooden bench with a high back

explanation.surface: Someone sitting on a bench is distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle someone is to disturb or upset them, a direct verbal synonym.

clue.text: Troublesome situation in fish pond

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a state of agitation
second meaning: an old word for a pond where fish are kept for eating

explanation.surface: Someone is in trouble in a fish pond.
explanation.definitionFit: Stew means both a state of worry and, in older English, a pond for keeping fish.

clue.text: Religious mystery showing in state capital, nothing less

indicators.note: less means minus, so the named letter is taken away

parts.note: Sacramento is the capital of California
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A religious mystery play is staged in an American state capital and nowhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing less' reads like 'no less than', but it means remove O.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrament is a sacred rite, and the Church describes sacraments as mysteries.

clue.text: Rather engaging term used in Queensland

definitions.text: Rather engaging term used in Queensland

parts.note: surface reading: a word that is quite charming or appealing
setter's reading: an engaging term is one used to engage someone, a friendly greeting heard in Australia

explanation.walkthrough: 'Engaging' means opening a conversation, not attractive; Queensland points to Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the standard informal Australian salutation, a greeting meaning hello.

clue.text: Sellers perhaps fastest to make a public statement

parts.note: Peter Sellers was one of the Goons, of the radio comedy The Goon Show
a record time is the fastest yet

explanation.surface: Peter Sellers, perhaps the quickest, makes a public announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sellers' looks like merchants; it is the comedian Peter Sellers.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on record is to state something officially and publicly.

clue.text: Face model after work

indicators.note: after places the model word behind the work word, fixing their order

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
to pose is to model for an artist

explanation.surface: A model goes to face the camera after finishing work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the model's word behind the work's.
explanation.definitionFit: To face someone in a contest is to oppose them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Tinder provided by one crazy man in Durban

parts.note: a means one
a direct synonym
ou is South African slang for a man or fellow; Durban is a South African city

explanation.surface: A dating app match is supplied by a mad South African man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tinder' looks like the dating app; here it is material that catches fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Amadou is a spongy fungus dried and used as kindling for lighting fires.

clue.text: Raising a tax shelter externally

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: externally means on the outside, so the shelter word wraps around the other

parts.note: a tent is a shelter
a toll is a levy

explanation.surface: Someone is raising a tax on tax shelters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax shelter' reads as one financial phrase; the words work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Attollent is an anatomical adjective for muscles that lift or raise a part.

clue.text: Bridge system in place not entirely backed

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the letters are read in reverse
not entirely means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: local can mean a particular place or locality

explanation.surface: A bridge player's bidding system is only partly supported locally.
explanation.walkthrough: Trim LOCAL to LOCA, then read it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Acol is the standard bidding convention used in British contract bridge.

clue.text: Rake over very small area below Italian mansion, bottom of garden

parts.note: casa is Italian for house

indicators.note: the bottom of a down entry's word is its last letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the final letter of garden
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
V is short for very
A is a short abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A garden rake goes over a tiny patch below an Italian villa's garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake' seems a garden tool; it is a womaniser. Over is a cricket term for six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Casanova, the Venetian adventurer, gives his name to any notorious seducer or libertine.

clue.text: Cattle pens time after time overturned? Almost

indicators.note: turning something over flips it, so the result is read backwards
to pen is to enclose, so the cattle word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: oxen are cattle
T is the abbreviation for time
a second T, for the second time

explanation.surface: Cattle are penned up and knocked over again and again, very nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: Put TT after the O of OXEN to get OTTXEN, then turn it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Next to is used to mean almost, as in 'next to impossible'.

clue.text: Play at once excited? I'm not sure

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: these letters rearranged
er is a hesitant sound of uncertainty

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to play at once, excitedly, then hesitates.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-acter is a short drama in a single act, a type of stage play.

clue.text: Jag seals about right for saloon worker?

indicators.note: to seal is to close something up inside, so one word holds the others

parts.note: a jag is a drinking spree, as is a bender
A is short for about, from Latin circa's sense
RT is an abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A Jaguar saloon car is fully sealed, roughly right for a salesman?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jag' and 'saloon' suggest Jaguar cars; a jag is a bout of drinking and the saloon is a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A bartender serves drinks in a bar, and a saloon is a bar, especially in the American West.

clue.text: Marshal reloading number of linked mines

indicators.note: to marshal is to arrange or order, so the letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A military marshal oversees the reloading of a string of connected mines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshal' looks like an army officer, but it is the instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A girandole, besides a branched candlestick, is a cluster of connected explosive charges fired together.

clue.text: Witness leaving with oddly small maps in the corner

indicators.note: oddly suggests something strange or out of order, so letters are rearranged
leaving means departing, so the named letter goes out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A witness departs, strangely clutching small maps in a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: Take W from WITNESS and rearrange ITNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Insets are smaller pictures or maps set within a larger one, often placed in a corner.

clue.text: Note on raw recruit Republican sent out for Congress

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for note

indicators.note: sending someone out removes them, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a rookie is a new recruit
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A new recruit's note about a Republican expelled from the US Congress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' and 'Republican' suggest American politics; congress here means sexual intercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Nookie is slang for sex, and congress is an old formal word for sexual intercourse.

clue.text: No Scottish banks make a loud noise for lady

indicators.note: banks are edges, so the first word lies on either side of the second

parts.note: nae is Scots for no
to din is to make a clamour

explanation.surface: No Scottish bank makes a fuss for a woman customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' suggests financial institutions; here the Scottish word flanks the noise word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadine is a woman's first name, and a lady is a woman.

clue.text: Insect up sticks caught

indicators.note: caught in the sense of heard or picked up by the ear

parts.note: to up sticks is to leave in a hurry, to flee

explanation.surface: An insect sets off but is caught.
explanation.walkthrough: To up sticks is a British idiom for suddenly moving away.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a small, wingless, jumping bloodsucking insect.

clue.text: Greek money as before left out for bulk carriers

indicators.note: out means removed, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: obols were coins of ancient Greece, hence 'as before'
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Old Greek coins are again left out as payment for cargo ships.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove L from OBOLS.
explanation.definitionFit: OBOs are ore-bulk-oil vessels, ships able to carry oil or dry cargo in bulk.

clue.text: What's turned up in morning-after pill box?

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means read from bottom to top, so backwards
in tells us the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run inside this word

explanation.surface: What turns up in an emergency contraceptive pill packet?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pill box' seems part of the morning-after pill scene but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An inro is a small Japanese lacquered case once worn at the waist to hold medicines.

clue.text: Free men close ranks originally to be different

indicators.note: becoming different means changing form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: originally points to the beginning, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of ranks

explanation.surface: Freed men close ranks, insisting on being different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close ranks' looks like one military phrase; the words work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceorls were the lowest rank of freemen in Anglo-Saxon England, free but not noble.

clue.text: Judge accommodates number previously cut

indicators.note: to accommodate is to give room to, so one word holds another inside

parts.note: to see is to judge or consider
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A judge makes room for a figure that was earlier reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Previously' marks the definition as an obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Snee is an archaic or dialect verb for to cut, now out of use.

clue.text: Narrow-minded on large island

parts.note: borné, from French, means limited in outlook
o' is a shortened form of on, as in o' nights

explanation.surface: A bigot is stranded on a big island.
explanation.definitionFit: Borneo is the third-largest island in the world, shared by three countries.

clue.text: Opening item in programme not started

indicators.note: not started means the beginning is missing, so the first letter goes

parts.note: an event is one item on a programme of activities

explanation.surface: The opening item of a programme has not yet begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening' looks like it describes the first item; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vent is an aperture or outlet through which air or gas escapes.

clue.text: Work out too much in public, then shower

parts.note: overt means done openly
a shower is a fall of rain

explanation.surface: A gym-goer exercises excessively in public, then has a shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower' looks like the post-workout wash but is the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtrain is to exercise beyond what the body can recover from.

clue.text: Heard order for starter is sweet

indicators.note: heard means we go by the sound of the words, not their spelling

parts.note: a race starter is ordered to say 'go'

explanation.surface: A diner hears an order for a first course being a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' looks like a first course; it is the person who starts a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago pudding is a traditional British dessert, and a sweet is a pudding course.

clue.text: Prearranged call top agent put out for spy

parts.note: set means fixed in advance

indicators.note: put out means expelled, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to term something is to call it
M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A prearranged phone call from a leading agent is cancelled to protect a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M from TERM and add it to SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter, in Chambers, is an informer or decoy who watches for a criminal, hence a spy.
